answer: A goal I am genuinely determined to achieve is to build a successful career in a field I am passionate about, rather than simply working for a salary. For me, that field is education, and more specifically helping students from small towns like Sirajganj get into good universities abroad. This matters to me because I believe finding your work meaningful is essential to a happy life. In my experience, a single good piece of advice at the right moment can change the direction of someone's life. I see many bright young people around me who have the ability but lack the right guidance, and I would love to help fill that gap. To achieve it, I am steadily developing my skills and gaining as much relevant experience as possible at the consultancy where I work. I also hope to do a master's degree abroad myself, so that I understand the whole journey first-hand. I know it will require patience and a lot of [[persistence]], as such things rarely happen overnight. I try to set myself small, [[attainable]] targets along the way to stay motivated. Honestly, the thought of one day doing work that I find genuinely [[fulfilling]] is incredibly motivating. If I achieved it, I think I would feel an enormous sense of pride and satisfaction, especially seeing former students thrive. It is not about wealth or status for me, but about purpose. I am fully aware the road will be [[arduous]], but I am prepared to put in the effort, because I believe it will be thoroughly worth it in the end.

followUps.q: Have you told your family about this goal?
followUps.answer: Yes, and they are very supportive. My father ran his own business for over thirty years, so he understands better than anyone what it takes to build something slowly and [[steadily]].

followUps.q: Do you think your goal might change in the future?
followUps.answer: The details might change, for example where I work or what my exact role is. But I think the core idea of helping young people make good decisions about their education will stay with me.

note: Made the field concrete (education consultancy, students from small towns), added his own study-abroad step; replaced plain 'challenging' with [[arduous]].
